concerns.text: The plan cites 'https://huggingface.co/datasets/jon-tow/okapi_arc_challenge/...' for ARC-Challenge evaluation. This is a third-party mirror, not the canonical source. The spec (FR-005) and Constitution (Principle I) require fetching from the canonical source to ensure reproducibility. The plan should cite 'allenai/ai2_arc' directly (as it does for the loader) and remove the reliance on the 'jon-tow' mirror URL which may drift or disappear.

The plan cites 'https://huggingface.co/datasets/stas/openwebtext-10k/...' as the verification URL for the BoolQ dataset. This is a mismatch: the URL points to an OpenWebText subset, not the BoolQ dataset. While the loader 'google/boolq' is correct, the verification URL is factually wrong and does not prove the BoolQ dataset is accessible. This undermines the 'Verified Datasets' claim for this resource.

The plan assumes GPT-2 124M training on 2 vCPU with batch size 4 will fit in ~7 GB RAM and complete 3 cycles in 12 hours. Training a 124M model for 1 epoch on 100k samples on 2 vCPUs is computationally infeasible within the 12-hour window (estimated >24-48 hours for a single epoch on CPU). The plan relies on 'streaming' which does not reduce the compute time required for the forward/backward passes. This compute assumption is incorrect for the stated hardware constraints.
